title: tiny-eye configuration
$comment: Generated by `make schemas` — do not edit; change the source of truth instead.
description: tiny-eye configuration file (merged over the built-in config/default.yaml).

id.description:
Node id, unique among the nodes sharing `storage.url`. With `region` it names the node's
object prefix `<region>/<id>/`; empty falls back to the default.

region.description:
Region label stamped on rows (one bucket per region, SPEC §12); first part of the node's
object prefix. Empty falls back to the default.

tenant.description: Tenant stamped on rows (single tenant in v1).

node.description: Identity of this node; tenant and region are stamped on every row it ingests.

server.description: HTTP listener (API, OTLP/HTTP, remote-write, Loki push, /metrics).

endpoint.description: Empty for AWS; e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:19000` for MinIO.

access_key_id.description: Secret: prefer the env var TINY_EYE__STORAGE__S3__ACCESS_KEY_ID.

secret_access_key.description: Secret: prefer the env var TINY_EYE__STORAGE__S3__SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.

storage.description: Object storage for Parquet data files and commit envelopes.

url.description:
A DuckDB file path, or `postgres:<libpq conninfo>` (then both fleet intervals must be `0s`:
a fleet publishes and reads catalog files).

catalog.description: DuckLake catalog holding table metadata and file lists.

wal_dir.description: Directory of the write-ahead log (durability: wal).

flush_bytes.description: Flush the open batch when it reaches this size...

max_sample_age.description: Samples older than this are rejected.

max_sample_future.description: Samples further ahead than this are rejected.

arena_limit.description: Above this many buffered bytes ingest answers 429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.

ingest.description: Write path: durability, flush thresholds, admission limits (SPEC §5).

checkpoint_interval.description: How often pending envelopes are applied to the catalog.

hot_grace.description: Keep committed rows in RAM this long after the catalog has them.

compaction_interval.description: How often closed hours are checked for compaction.

compaction_delay.description: Compact an hour this long after it closes.

retention.description: Data older than this is deleted.

snapshot_grace.description:
A catalog snapshot is expired once a newer one has existed this long; only then are the
files no newer snapshot references deleted. At least `fleet.publish_interval + 2 ×
fleet.refresh_interval + query.timeout`, so a catalog copy another node may still be
reading never names a deleted file (readers drop a copy older than the smaller of their own
and the publisher's grace minus their refresh interval and query timeout).

publish_interval.description: Publish a copy of this node's catalog to `_fleet/` in object storage this often; `0s` = never.

refresh_interval.description:
Look for the catalog copies of other nodes sharing `storage.url` this often and query their
data with this node's; `0s` = never. Copies too old to be safe are skipped (see
`coordinator.snapshot_grace`).

dir.description:
Local directory for downloaded catalog copies: they live in `<dir>/<node.id>/` (this node's
id), which is emptied at start.

max_copy_bytes.description:
A catalog copy of another node that unpacks to more than this is refused (copies come from
shared storage and are not trusted).

fleet.description: Nodes sharing `storage.url`: publish this node's catalog copy, query the others' copies.

timeout.description: A query taking longer from arrival (waiting for a free connection included) is interrupted.

workers.description: DuckDB connections serving queries in parallel.

auth.description: Bearer-token auth; scopes per operation come from api/openapi.yaml (`x-scope`).

dir.description: Directory of dashboard YAML files (schema: schema/generated/dashboard.schema.json).

dashboards.description: Dashboards loaded from YAML files at start.

path.description:
Node-local DuckDB file holding materialized points; empty keeps them in memory (they are
derived data: losing them only means computing the uncovered range again).

resolution.description: Step of the stored points. A read whose step is a multiple of it uses them.

settle.description:
A step is stored once it is this old. A sample that arrives later than this for a stored
step makes the next tick recompute the stored steps from its timestamp on, so stored points
never miss accepted data; a larger value stores later and recomputes less often.

max_panels.description:
At most this many panels are materialized; the rest are skipped with a warning. Bounds the
store: `max_panels * max_points_per_panel * ~24 B`.

max_points_per_panel.description:
Stored points kept per panel. Past it the oldest steps are dropped (a read computes them
again), so a wide panel (many series per step) cannot grow the store without bound. A
panel that cannot hold at least 240 steps (1 h at 15 s) is not stored at all.

max_slice_points.description:
Points one background slice may produce (computed and written in one statement). The
slice length adapts to the panel's width, so the working memory of a tick stays bounded.

materialize.description: Materialized dashboard panels (`materialize: true` on a panel).

Node id, unique among the nodes sharing `storage.url`. With `region` it names the node's
object prefix `<region>/<id>/`; empty falls back to the default.
